summary: This document defines a collection of common data types in the YANG data modeling language. They are designed to be imported by other YANG modules written in the routing area, so each module does not have to redefine them.

eli5.summary: It is a box of standard building blocks, like names for common kinds of values, that routing-related data models can borrow instead of inventing again.

questions: what is a route target in yang
what yang types exist for mpls labels
subtitle: A shared toolbox of YANG data types so routing models do not each reinvent router IDs, route targets, timers and MPLS labels.

tldr.problem: Many routing-area YANG modules need the same kinds of values, such as router identifiers, BGP route targets, timers and MPLS labels. Defining them separately in each module would waste effort and lead to inconsistencies.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8294 defines two YANG modules of derived types and groupings, ietf-routing-types and iana-routing-types, that other modules import.
tldr.outcome: Routing models can reuse one agreed set of definitions. The IANA-maintained module is meant to track two IANA registries as they change.

today: RFC 8294 is a Proposed Standard (December 2017) and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It remains the definition of these routing types.

sections.title: Why Common Routing Types
sections.content:
YANG (RFC 6020, RFC 7950) is a data modeling language used to model configuration data, state data, Remote Procedure Calls and notifications for network management protocols. It has a small set of built-in types and lets authors derive new ones from them.

RFC 8294 collects derived types that are applicable to modeling in the routing area. The goal stated in the abstract is that other modules defined in the routing area import them.
sections.eli5: Everyone who writes a routing data model needs the same few kinds of values. This document writes them down once so people can share them.

sections.title: Two Modules, One Split
sections.content:
The document defines two YANG modules. ietf-routing-types holds common routing types that do not correspond directly to IANA mappings. iana-routing-types holds types that map directly onto IANA registries. The only imports in the first module are ietf-yang-types and ietf-inet-types, both from RFC 6991.

Besides types, the IETF module defines two groupings, which are reusable collections of schema nodes: mpls-label-stack and vpn-route-targets.
sections.eli5: There are two boxes. One has general routing blocks. The other has blocks that copy official lists kept by IANA.

sections.title: VPN and Router Identity Types
sections.content:
router-id identifies nodes in routing and other control-plane protocols. It is a 32-bit number in dotted-quad format that uniquely identifies the router within an Autonomous System.

Several types support BGP/MPLS VPNs (RFC 4364). A route-target controls distribution of VRF information and is an 8-octet BGP extended community. Its text form is type:administrator:assigned-number, with patterns for types 0, 1, 2 and 6 and a generic pattern for future types; examples given are 0:100:100 and 1:1.1.1.1:100. ipv6-route-target is the 20-octet IPv6 Address Specific form (RFC 5701).

route-target-type gives import, export or both rules. route-distinguisher identifies separate routes, VPNs and VRFs, and route-origin and ipv6-route-origin indicate the Site of Origin.
sections.eli5: A router ID is a name tag for a router. Route targets and route distinguishers are colored stickers that keep different companies' private networks sorted out.

sections.title: Multicast, Timer and Numeric Types
sections.content:
For multicast, the module defines ipv4-multicast-group-address (224.0.0.0 to 239.255.255.255), ipv6-multicast-group-address (ff00::/8) and a version-neutral ip-multicast-group-address. The multicast source address types also allow a wildcard source, written as an asterisk.

Timer types cover values set in seconds, not set, or set to infinity: timer-value-seconds16 (range 1 to 65535), timer-value-seconds32 and timer-value-milliseconds (both 1 to 4294967295). timer-multiplier is a uint8 counting how many timer intervals may pass before a failure is assumed, as with BFD packets.

Other types include link-access-type (broadcast, non-broadcast-multiaccess, point-to-multipoint, point-to-point), bandwidth-ieee-float32, percentage (0 to 100), timeticks64 and uint24 (0 to 16777215).
sections.eli5: These blocks describe things like how long to wait before deciding a neighbor has gone quiet, what kind of link two routers share, and numbers with sensible limits.

sections.title: MPLS Label Types
sections.content:
The 20-bit label value in an MPLS label stack is specified in RFC 3032. The YANG types here cover only that value, not the Traffic Class and TTL encodings.

mpls-label-general-use has range 16 to 1048575, which excludes special-purpose values. mpls-label-special-purpose is an identityref based on identities such as ipv4-explicit-null-label, router-alert-label, ipv6-explicit-null-label, implicit-null-label, entropy-label-indicator, gal-label, oam-alert-label and extension-label. mpls-label is the union of both. generalized-label represents a GMPLS label (RFC 3471) and does not identify its own type, which is known from context.
sections.eli5: MPLS labels are like numbered tickets on a package. Some numbers are reserved for special jobs, and the rest are for everyday use.

sections.title: The IANA-Maintained Module
sections.content:
iana-routing-types defines address-family and bgp-safi (subsequent address family) enumerations. They reflect the IANA "Address Family Numbers" and "Subsequent Address Family Identifiers (SAFI) Parameters" registries; for example ipv4 is value 1 and ipv6 is value 2 as address families.

Entries must not be added to the module directly. They must be added to the registries first, and then a new enum statement and a new revision statement must be added to the module. IANA added notes to both registries pointing to this rule. The document also registers the namespaces and module names for both modules.
sections.eli5: The second box is a copy of two official lists. If the official list grows, the copy must be updated to match, but nobody may change the copy first.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The definitions themselves have no security or privacy impact on the Internet. Impact can come from how concrete YANG modules use them. The security considerations of YANG 1.1 (RFC 7950) apply.
sections.eli5: The building blocks are harmless on their own. What matters is what people build with them.
